name: Blacklisted
label: Deathwish
lede: Philadelphia hardcore that ran about twenty minutes a record, tuned low, and written by a singer who kept quitting and kept coming back.

eras.title: A Philly basement band finds Deathwish
eras.text: George Hirsch and friends start Blacklisted in Philadelphia in 2003. Two years and a split later, they are on Deathwish Inc. and have a first full-length in the racks.

years.h: Blacklisted start in Philadelphia with a 7-inch
years.p: [[George Hirsch|2a18a939-02e7-4a7f-9dd3-bbef0ff83925]] sings; the band's first releases are a self-titled 7-inch and the Our Youth Is Wasted EP on Stillborn.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia the original line-up was Hirsch on vocals, Jon Nean and Tim Smith on guitar and bass, and Zach Trotta on drums. Later interviews describe Smith as the main songwriter and Trotta as the drummer he replaced on the first album.

years.h: Dead Man's Hand: 3, a split with First Blood
years.p: The Deathwish split with the California band First Blood is how [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]]'s label first meets Blacklisted.
years.xp: George Hirsch told No Echo that the Deathwish crew came to the studio to see the band after the split and were supportive. Deathwish lists the release as Dead Man's Hand: 3.

years.h: ...The Beat Goes On: 13 songs in about 24 minutes
years.p: Blacklisted's first full-length for Deathwish is recorded with engineer Jim Seigel in bursts of two or three weeks between tours.
years.xp: Hirsch told No Echo that Tim Smith and Shawn Foley wrote the music together in a jam room over a few weeks, and that the band tuned down to C, taking cues from Turmoil and Buried Alive. He also said he was unhappy with the record at first, then came to see how hard Smith and Foley had worked under pressure.

eras.title: Heavier than heaven
eras.text: A near-breakup and a lost songwriter, then the two records that make the case: a short EP and a 19-minute album recorded with Kurt Ballou.

years.h: Blacklisted nearly break up and lose Tim Smith's songwriting
years.p: Hirsch told Scene Point Blank the band came close to ending in 2006 after losing a key songwriting member.
years.xp: The band carried on with Hirsch, Shawn Foley, Dave Walling and a rotating guitar slot. In later interviews Hirsch said he has quit the band many times to sort things out.

years.h: Peace on Earth, War on Stage: four songs, six minutes
years.p: The 7-inch on Deathwish (DWI58) is pressed in 3,000 copies according to Wikipedia; two songs are later re-recorded for the next album.
play: Peace on Earth, War on Stage

years.cap: Heavier Than Heaven, Lonelier Than God, Deathwish DWI70
years.src: Wikipedia · No Echo · Scene Point Blank
years.h: Heavier Than Heaven, Lonelier Than God, with Kurt Ballou
years.p: Eleven songs in 19 minutes 37 seconds, produced by [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] and mastered by Alan Douches.
years.xp:
The album is the record most fans and the band's own reviewers point to as Blacklisted's best. No Echo calls it one of the best hardcore releases of its decade. Hirsch told Scene Point Blank that the title nods to the name of Nirvana's first European tour.

The band planned tours of Australia, Mexico, Central and South America and Japan around the record, and Hirsch described himself as having toured into a Twilight Zone type of vortex.

years.h: No One Deserves to Be Here More Than Me adds violin and trumpet
years.p: Recorded with engineer Will Yip, the 14-song album (DWI100) brings in violin, trumpet, rainstick and backing vocals from Melissa Farley.
years.xp: Hirsch later called it the band's most definitive record in a Punknews interview. The CD carried three bonus tracks from the Eccentrichine EP.
play: No One Deserves to Be Here More Than Me

eras.title: Hiatus, a solo record and one more album
eras.text: Family and life slow the band down. Hirsch records folk under another name, gets through a hard year, and Blacklisted return with a fourth album.

years.p: A short EP released between the second and third albums, later folded into the CD of No One Deserves to Be Here More Than Me.

years.h: George Hirsch goes acoustic as Harm Wülf
years.p: His solo album There's Honey In the Soil So We Wait for the Till... is dark folk, released while Blacklisted sit quiet.
years.xp: A second Harm Wülf record, Hijrah, followed in 2016 with cover art from a photograph Hirsch took of the Sólheimasandur plane wreck in Iceland. Hirsch has since released music as Rose Clouds and returned to hardcore with Staticlone.

years.h: The band goes on hold while Hirsch struggles
years.p: Hirsch told Punknews in 2015 that Blacklisted paused the year before during a mental health crisis, and credited promoter Joe Hardcore for support.
years.xp: The same interview places Blacklisted at This Is Hardcore in August 2014 and mentions a European run through Iceland and Finland. Hirsch said he had quit the band about fifty times.

years.cap: When People Grow, People Go, Deathwish DW169
years.h: When People Grow, People Go ends a six-year wait
years.p: Will Yip produces 11 songs in just over 20 minutes; "Deeper Kind" streams in December 2014 and "Turn in the Pike" gets a video.
years.xp: Writing began in late 2013. Wikipedia describes the record as blending the band's experimental and hardcore sides after a 2012 EP.

years.h: Last shows, for the 10th anniversary of Heavier Than Heaven
years.p: Blacklisted play what turns out to be their last shows for five years, built around the 2008 album.

eras.title: Back for Unbroken
eras.text: After five quiet years, Blacklisted return for one basement show. The reason is a friend's request, not a comeback plan.

years.h: The Philadelphia show with Unbroken is announced
years.p: Blacklisted are billed to play with the reunited Unbroken and Damnation A.D. at First Unitarian Church; Wikipedia says it sold out in under a minute and a second night was added.

years.big: Five years off. Six hundred in a basement.
q: The only reason we're here tonight is because Unbroken asked us.
years.p: Stereogum reports a sold-out room of about 600, an opening "Tourist" from ...The Beat Goes On and a cover of Ink & Dagger's "Full Circle".
years.xp: The set leaned on Heavier Than Heaven, Lonelier Than God and closed with "Wish". Hirsch told the crowd why they were there.

years.h: Hirsch lends his voice to other bands
years.p: He has contributed vocals or lyrics to tracks by [[Ceremony|c13da818-d566-4f2a-aaaf-1c68301ddc43]], [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], Cold World, Defeater and Nails.
years.xp: Hirsch also fronts Staticlone. In No Echo's 2023 interview he said no new Blacklisted material was planned and that the band had no further tours in view.

sources.title: No Echo: making of ...The Beat Goes On
